title: Temurah 27
description: The two meanings of “in place of,” Rava and Rav Ashi on a blemished consecrated animal and where the owner’s hand rests, the unresolved dilemmas of Abaye and Rav Ashi about several animals exchanged at once, Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish on paying the Temple the difference in value, Ulla on an assessment by three, and the mishna that closes chapter 5 on “in place of a burnt offering” and animals declared “for a burnt offering.”
topics: 🔄 Taḥat: associating sanctity, as with the leprous spot, or desacralizing, as with Isaiah’s brass and gold
✋ Rava and Rav Ashi: a blemished consecrated animal, and where the owner’s hand rests
🐑 Two, three and four animals at once: does a person abandon the permitted way? The dilemmas stand unresolved
⚖️ Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish: paying the Temple the difference, by Torah law or by rabbinic law
🔁 Reverse the attributions? Rabbi Yirmeya and Rabbi Yona, Shmuel’s maneh for a peruta, and Rav Ḥisda
👥 Ulla: an assessment by three stands even against a hundred, and Rav Safra’s objection
📜 Mishna: “in place of a burnt offering” says nothing; “for a burnt offering” means its value
📖 Hadran: chapter 5, Keitzad Ma’arimin, ends; chapter 6, Kol HaAsurin, comes next

a2.he: דְּאַחוֹלֵי, דִּכְתִיב: ״תַּחַת הַנְּחוֹשֶׁת אָבִיא זָהָב״, וְהִלְכָּךְ, גַּבֵּי קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ דְּעָבְדִין תְּמוּרָה — לִישָּׁנָא דְּאַתְפּוֹסֵי הוּא, גַּבֵּי קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת דְּלָא עָבְדִין תְּמוּרָה — לִישָּׁנָא דְּאַחוֹלֵי הוּא.

a3.he: אָמַר רָבָא: אֲפִילּוּ בְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ לִישָּׁנָא דְּאַחוֹלֵי הוּא, כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה הֶקְדֵּשׁ בַּעַל מוּם.

a4.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אָשֵׁי: אֲפִילּוּ בְּבַעַל מוּם נָמֵי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ לִישָּׁנָא דְּאַחוֹלֵי, וּמַשְׁכַּחַת לִישָּׁנָא דְּאַתְפּוֹסֵי. יָדוֹ אַקּוֹדֶשׁ — חוֹל הָוֵי, יָדוֹ אַחוֹל — קוֹדֶשׁ הָוֵי.

a5.he: בָּעֵי אַבָּיֵי: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ בַּעֲלוֹת מוּם, וּשְׁתֵּי בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל חוּלִּין תְּמִימוֹת, וְאָמַר ״הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ תַּחַת אֵלּוּ״, מַהוּ?

a6.he: מִי אָמַר לְאַתְפּוֹסֵי וְלָקֵי, אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא הֶיתֵּרָא — לָא שָׁבֵיק אִינִישׁ הֶיתֵּרָא וְעָבֵיד אִיסּוּרָא?

a7.he: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר, כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא הֶיתֵּרָא לָא שָׁבֵיק אִינִישׁ וְעָבֵיד אִיסּוּרָא, הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ, וְאַחַת מֵהֶן בַּעֲלַת מוּם, וּשְׁתֵּי בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל חוּלִּין, וְאַחַת מֵהֶן בַּעֲלַת מוּם, וְאָמַר ״הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ תַּחַת אֵלּוּ״, מַהוּ?

a8.he: מִי אָמַר: תְּמִימָה תַּחַת תְּמִימָה — לְאַתְפּוֹסֵי, בַּעֲלַת מוּם תַּחַת בַּעֲלַת מוּם — לְאַחוֹלֵי.

a9.he: אוֹ דִלְמָא, תְּמִימָה דְּחוּלִּין תַּחַת בַּעֲלַת מוּם דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ, בַּעֲלַת מוּם דְּחוּלִּין תַּחַת תְּמִימָה דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ, וְתַרְוַיְיהוּ לָקֵי?

a10.he: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר, כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא הֶיתֵּירָא — לָא עָבֵיד אִיסּוּרָא, וּלְאַחוֹלֵי הוּא, וְלָא לָקֵי. הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שָׁלֹשׁ בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ, וְאַחַת מֵהֶן בַּעֲלַת מוּם, וְשָׁלֹשׁ בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל חוּלִּין תְּמִימוֹת, וְאָמַר: ״הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ תַּחַת אֵלּוּ״.

a11.he: מִי אָמְרִינַן, מִדִּתְמִימוֹת תַּחַת תְּמִימוֹת לְאַתְפּוֹסֵי, תְּמִימוֹת נָמֵי תַּחַת בַּעֲלַת מוּם לְאַתְפּוֹסֵי? אוֹ דִלְמָא, הָכָא נָמֵי, כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא הֶיתֵּירָא לָא עָבֵיד אִיסּוּרָא, וְהַהִיא בָּתְרָיְיתָא לְאַחוֹלֵי הָוֵי.

a12.he: וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר, הָכָא נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּאַכַּתִּי גַּבְרָא לָא אִיתַּחְזַק בְּאִיסּוּרֵי, לָא שָׁבֵיק הֶתֵּירָא וְעָבֵיד אִיסּוּרָא. בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו אַרְבַּע בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ וְאַחַת מֵהֶן בַּעֲלַת מוּם, וְאַרְבַּע בְּהֵמוֹת שֶׁל חוּלִּין, וְאָמַר ״הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ תַּחַת אֵלּוּ״, מַהוּ?

a13.he: הָכָא וַדַּאי, כֵּיוָן דְּאִיתַּחְזַק גַּבְרָא בְּאִיסּוּרֵי (בְּכוּלָּן), לָקֵי בְּאַרְבַּע מַלְקִיּוֹת.

a14.he: אוֹ דִלְמָא, אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיתַּחְזַק בְּאִיסּוּרָא, לָא שָׁבֵיק אִינִישׁ הֶיתֵּירָא וְעָבֵיד אִיסּוּרָא, וְהָוֵי בָּתְרָיְיתָא לְאַחוֹלֵי הָוֵי? תֵּיקוּ.

a15.he: אִם הָיָה הֶקְדֵּשׁ בַּעַל מוּם יֹצֵא לְחוּלִּין כּוּ׳.

a16.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: יֹצֵא לְחוּלִּין דְּבַר תּוֹרָה, וְצָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּמִים מִדִּבְרֵיהֶם, וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אַף צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּמִים דְּבַר תּוֹרָה.

a17.he: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִי נֵימָא אַאוֹנָאָה, בְּהָא נֵימָא רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אַף צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּמִים דְּבַר תּוֹרָה?

a18.he: וְהָא תְנַן: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אוֹנָאָה: הָעֲבָדִים, וְהַשְּׁטָרוֹת, וְהַקַּרְקָעוֹת, וְהַהֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת!

a19.he: אֶלָּא, אַבִּטּוּל מִקָּח בְּהָא נֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּמִים מִדִּבְרֵיהֶם?

b1.he: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אַקַּרְקָעוֹת דְּחוּלִּין, וְרַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר אַהֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת, תַּרְוַויְיהוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמְרִי: אוֹנָאָה אֵין לָהֶן, בִּיטּוּל מִקָּח יֵשׁ לָהֶם!

b3.he: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ אֵיפוֹךְ? הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אַהֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן אַקַּרְקָעוֹת.

b4.he: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אַקַּרְקָעוֹת, אֲבָל הֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת אֵין לָהֶן בִּיטּוּל מִקָּח, הֵיכִי אֵיפוֹךְ לְהָא?

b6.he: לֵימָא בְּדִשְׁמוּאֵל קָא מִיפַּלְגִי, דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֶקְדֵּשׁ שָׁוֶה מָנֶה שֶׁחִילְּלוֹ עַל שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה מְחוּלָּל. דְּרַבִּי יוֹנָה לֵית לֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אִית לֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל.

b7.he: לָא, בֵּין דְּמָר וּבֵין דְּמָר — אִית לֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּרַבִּי יוֹנָה סָבַר: כִּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל — דִּיעֲבַד, אֲבָל לְכַתְּחִלָּה לָא אָמַר, וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה סָבַר: אֲפִילּוּ לְכַתְּחִלָּה.

b8.he: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, לְעוֹלָם לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ, וּדְקָא קַשְׁיָא לָךְ מַתְנִיתִין ״אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים... הֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת״ — כִּדְרַב חִסְדָּא.

b9.he: דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֵין לָהֶן אוֹנָאָה — אֵינָן בְּתוֹרַת אוֹנָאָה, דַּאֲפִילּוּ פָּחוֹת מִכְּדֵי אוֹנָאָה חוֹזֵר.

b10.he: אָמַר עוּלָּא: לָא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא בְּשָׁמוּי בִּתְרֵי, אֲבָל בְּשָׁמוּי בִּתְלָתָא, וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָתֵי בְּמֵאָה — לָא הָדַר.

b11.he: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב סָפְרָא: הֵיכָא אָמְרִינַן מְאָה כִּתְרֵי וּתְרֵי כִּמְאָה? לְעִנְיַן עֵדוּת, אֲבָל לְעִנְיַן אוּמְדָּנָא — בָּתַר דֵּעוֹת אָזְלִינַן.

b12.he: וְתוּ תְּלָתָא וּתְלָתָא, לָא אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר בָּתְרָא? דְּיַד הֶקְדֵּשׁ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה!

b13.he: קָסָבַר עוּלָּא: צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּמִים מִדִּבְרֵיהֶם, וְכֹל דְּרַבָּנַן אַקִּילוּ בֵּהּ רַבָּנַן.

b14.he: מַתְנִי׳ ״הֲרֵי זוֹ תַּחַת עוֹלָה״, ״תַּחַת חַטָּאת״ — לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם. ״תַּחַת חַטָּאת זוֹ״, וְ״תַחַת עוֹלָה זוֹ״, ״תַּחַת חַטָּאת וְתַחַת עוֹלָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי בַּבַּיִת״ — הָיָה לוֹ, דְּבָרָיו קַיָּימִים.

b15.he: אָמַר עַל הַבְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה וְעַל בַּעֲלַת מוּם ״הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ עוֹלָה״ — לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם. ״הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ לְעוֹלָה״ — יִמָּכְרוּ, וְיָבִיא בִּדְמֵיהֶם עוֹלָה.

b16.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּאִי כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר — הָא אֵין אָדָם מוֹצִיא דְּבָרָיו לְבַטָּלָה.

b17.he: ״הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ לְעוֹלָה״ — יִמָּכְרוּ וְיָבִיא בִּדְמֵיהֶן עוֹלָה. טַעְמָא דִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה וּבַעֲלַת מוּם, דְּלָא חַזְיָין — לָא בָּעֲיָין מוּמָא, אֲבָל מַפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְאָשָׁם אוֹ לְעוֹלָה — בָּעֲיָין מוּמָא.

b18.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: תִּימָּכֵר שֶׁלֹּא בְּמוּם.

messages.text: Continued from 26b: the mishna taught that “This is hereby in place of [taḥat] that” makes a substitute, yet a baraita teaches that with an animal consecrated for Temple maintenance the same words desacralize it. Abaye answered that taḥat is sometimes a term of associating one sanctity with another and sometimes a term of desacralization. It is a term of association, as it is written:

“But if the white leprous spot stays in its place [taḥteha]” (Leviticus 13:23). In this verse, the word “taḥteha” indicates that the white leprous spot remains in its place. This usage of the word is fitting for substitution, since when sanctity is transferred by substitution from a consecrated animal to a non-sacred animal, the sanctity of the consecrated animal remains in place, despite the fact that the non-sacred animal is also consecrated.

verse.he: וְאִם־תַּחְתֶּיהָ תַּעֲמֹד הַבַּהֶרֶת לֹא פָשָׂתָה צָרֶבֶת הַשְּׁחִין הִוא וְטִהֲרוֹ הַכֹּהֵן׃ {ס}
verse.en: But if the discoloration remains stationary, not having spread, it is the scar of the inflammation; the priest shall pronounce them pure.

notes.he: עמדה במקומה והיינו דומיא דאתפוסי שההקדש עומד במקומו הלכך הואיל ותרוייהו משמע לא מסרו הכתוב אלא לחכמים דידעי למימר היכא הוי תחת אתפוסי והיכא הוי חילול:
notes.en: “But if the white leprous spot stays in its place [taḥteha]”: it stood in its place, and this is analogous to association, in which the consecrated animal stands in its place. Therefore, since both [meanings] are implied, Scripture handed it over only to the Sages, who know how to say where taḥat means association and where it means desacralization.

notes.he: בתמורה דכתיב ואם תחתיה תעמוד הבהרת. כלומר שבמקומה עומדת [אף] בהמה זו של קודש במקומה בקדושתה ותופסת אחרת בקדושתה כדכתיב והיה הוא ותמורתו יהיה קודש:
notes.en: It implies an expression of association, in substitution, as it is written: “But if the white leprous spot stays in its place”: that is, it stands in its place. [So too] this consecrated animal stands in its place, in its sanctity, and takes hold of another in its sanctity, as it is written: “Then both it and its substitute shall be sacred” (Leviticus 27:10).

messages.text: Yet taḥat is also a term that indicates desacralization, as it is written: “In place of [taḥat] brass I will bring gold, and in place of iron I will bring silver, and in place of wood brass, and in place of stones iron” (Isaiah 60:17). In this verse, taḥat means replacement, which is what occurs in desacralization, where one item is replaced by another.

verse.he: תַּחַת הַנְּחֹשֶׁת אָבִיא זָהָב וְתַחַת הַבַּרְזֶל אָבִיא כֶסֶף וְתַחַת הָעֵצִים נְחֹשֶׁת וְתַחַת הָאֲבָנִים בַּרְזֶל וְשַׂמְתִּי פְקֻדָּתֵךְ שָׁלוֹם וְנֹגְשַׂיִךְ צְדָקָה׃
verse.en:
Instead of copper I will bring gold,
Instead of iron I will bring silver;
Instead of wood, copper—
And instead of stone, iron.
And I will appoint Well-being as your government,
Prosperity as your officials.

notes.he: שמוציאו מקדושתו ונכנס זה במקומו כדכתיב תחת הנחשת שגזלו אביא זהב במקומו הואיל וכן כו':
notes.en: And it implies an expression of desacralization: that it removes it from its sanctity and this one enters in its place, as it is written: “In place of the brass” that they stole “I will bring gold” in its place. Since this is so, etc.

messages.text: And therefore, the term should be understood in accordance with the context: With regard to animals consecrated for sacrifice upon the altar, which render a non-sacred animal for which they are exchanged a substitute, taḥat is a term that indicates the associating of one sanctity with another. With regard to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, which do not render a non-sacred animal for which they are exchanged a substitute, taḥat is a term that indicates desacralization.

notes.he: גבי קדשי בדק הבית כו':
notes.en: With regard to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, etc. [Rashi cites the words without further comment.]

messages.text: Even with regard to animals consecrated for sacrifice upon the altar, which render a non-sacred animal for which they are exchanged a substitute, you can find that taḥat is a term that indicates desacralization. For example, in a case where a consecrated animal was blemished and can be desacralized because it is unfit to be sacrificed, and one placed that consecrated animal next to a non-sacred animal and said: This animal is in place of [taḥat] that animal. Although the blemished sacred animal can render a non-sacred animal for which it is exchanged consecrated as a substitute, in this context the term taḥat means desacralization.
messages.quote: With regard to animals consecrated for sacrifice upon the altar … taḥat is a term that indicates the associating

notes.he: אמר רבא אפילו בקדשי מזבח הוי לישנא דאחולי כגון שהיה הקודש בעל מום [בהכי] סבירא ליה לרבא דהא ואם היה קדש בעל מום משמע נמי (אחולי) [ארישא קאי אמר ה"ז תחת זו] שהרי לא מצינו תחת גבי תמורה:
notes.en: Rava said: Even with animals consecrated for the altar it is an expression of desacralization, for example where the consecrated animal was blemished. Rava holds [so] because [the mishna’s] “And if the consecrated animal was blemished” also refers back to the first clause, where he said: This is hereby in place of that, for we do not find taḥat [stated] with regard to substitution. [Translated following the bracketed correction in the printed text.]

messages.text: Even in the case of a blemished animal, mentioned by Rava, sometimes you find that taḥat is a term that indicates desacralization and sometimes you find that taḥat is a term that indicates the associating of one sanctity with another.
messages.quote: where a consecrated animal was blemished

notes.dh: הניח ידו על הקדש בעל מום
notes.he: ואמר תהא זו של חולין תחת זו של קדש (שירי) [שיתחלל] עליו חול היינו משמע לישנא דאחולי שיצא של קודש ויכנס זה במקומו:
notes.en: He placed his hand on the blemished consecrated animal and said: Let this non-sacred one be in place of this consecrated one, that it be desacralized onto it: [it is] non-sacred. That is what an expression of desacralization implies: that the consecrated one goes out and this one enters in its place.

messages.text: If the owner’s hand is resting on the consecrated animal and he says: This animal is in place of [taḥat] that animal, it is a term of desacralization, as the placement of his hand indicates that his intention is to desacralize the consecrated animal, with its sanctity transferred to that non-sacred animal.

notes.he: הניח ידו אקודש ואמר זו תחת זו אידך דחולין ודאי לחולין מתכוין וחול הוא:
notes.en: His hand on the consecrated animal, it is non-sacred: he placed his hand on the consecrated animal and said: This is in place of this. [As for] the other, the non-sacred one, he certainly intends [the consecrated one] to become non-sacred, and it is non-sacred.

messages.text: If the owner’s hand is resting on the non-sacred animal when he says: This animal is in place of that animal, then taḥat is a term of substitution, as the placement of his hand indicates that his intention is for the non-sacred animal to be consecrated with the same sanctity as the consecrated animal.

notes.he: ואמר זו תחת זו אתפוסי הוא דקדש בעל מום עושה תמורה ואי הוה בעי האי לאחולי הוה מנח ידיה על ההיא דקדש:
notes.en: His hand on the non-sacred animal: and he said: This is in place of this, it is association, for a blemished consecrated animal renders a substitute; and had he wanted to desacralize it, he would have placed his hand on the consecrated one.

notes.dh: אם הניח ידו על זו של חולין ואמר תהא זו תחת זו
notes.he: הוי האי בעל מום קודש ולא יצא לחולין וזה תמורתו:
notes.en: If he placed his hand on this non-sacred one and said: Let this be in place of this, this blemished one remains consecrated and does not go out to non-sacred status, and this is its substitute.

messages.text: If there were standing before him two sacrificial animals that were blemished and two non-sacred animals that were unblemished, and, without placing his hands on any animal, he says: These animals are hereby in place of [taḥat] those animals, what is the halakha?

notes.he: ולא הניח ידו לא כאן ולא כאן:
notes.en: And he said: These are hereby in place of those: and he did not place his hand either here or there. [Rashi’s heading has the stray word “sin offering” in parentheses, marked for deletion.]

notes.dh: בעי רב אשי היו לפניו שתי בהמות
notes.he: ה"ה דבחד בהמת קדש בעלת מום וחד תמימה חולין מצי למיבעי ואיידי דאיכא בסמוך בעיות דמיירי דוקא בשתי בהמות נקט נמי הכא כן:
notes.en: Rav Ashi raises a dilemma: If there were before him two animals: [Tosafot’s text reads Rav Ashi here, where ours reads Abaye.] The same dilemma could have been raised about one blemished consecrated animal and one unblemished non-sacred animal; but since the dilemmas that follow deal specifically with two animals, it took this case here too.

messages.text: Did he intend to say taḥat as association, i.e., to consecrate the two non-sacred animals as substitutes, and therefore he is flogged two sets of lashes for the two violations of the prohibition against consecrating an animal as a substitute?
messages.quote: These animals are hereby in place of those animals, what is the halakha?

notes.he: מתכוין או לאחולי מתכוין. והוא הדין נמי דמצי למיבעי בחדא אלא איידי דבעי מיבעיא הך בעיא אחריתי בתרתי נקט סירכא דתרתי:
notes.en: To associate: does he intend to associate, or does he intend to desacralize? And the same dilemma could have been raised about a single [pair]; but since it wishes to raise another dilemma about two, it took up the pattern of two [here too].

notes.he: בתמורה קאמר ולקי תרי מלקיות:
notes.en: Do we say to associate: he means in substitution, and he is flogged two sets of lashes.

messages.text: Or perhaps, does one say that since anywhere that there exists both a permitted and a prohibited manner to perform an action, a person does not cast aside the permitted manner and perform the prohibition? If so, here too his intention was to desacralize the two blemished animals, and therefore he is not flogged.

notes.he: לא ימיר:
notes.en: The prohibition: [of] “He shall not substitute it” (Leviticus 27:10).

notes.he: או דלמא כל היכא דאיכא היתירא דיכיל לאחולי דלית ביה לאו ועביד איסורא להמיר:
notes.en: Or perhaps wherever there is a permitted way, that he can desacralize, which involves no prohibition, would he perform the prohibition of substituting?

messages.text: And if you say that anywhere that there exists both a permitted and a prohibited manner to perform an action, a person does not cast aside the permitted manner and perform the prohibition, in a case where there were standing before him two sacrificial animals, one of which was blemished and one of which was unblemished, and two non-sacred animals, one of which was blemished and one of which was unblemished, and he said: These animals are hereby in place of [taḥat] those animals, what is the halakha? Although he certainly intended to transfer the sanctity of the unblemished sacrificial animal to a non-sacred animal by substitution, it is unclear which of the two non-sacred animals he intended to consecrate as a substitute.

Did he intend to say that the unblemished non-sacred animal should be consecrated as a substitute in place of the unblemished consecrated animal, and with regard to this pairing he intended to associate the sanctity by substitution, while the blemished non-sacred animal should be consecrated in place of the blemished consecrated animal, and for this pairing he intended to desacralize the consecrated animal. If so, he is flogged only for the first pairing and not for the second pairing.
messages.quote: two sacrificial animals, one of which was blemished … and two non-sacred animals, one of which was blemished

notes.he: דהא ודאי אי אפשר דלא הויא חדא לאתפוסי הואיל וחדא תמימה דהקדש איכא מיהת בקדשי מזבח ותמימים אמרינן לעיל דאתפוסי הוא:
notes.en: Unblemished in place of unblemished, to associate: for it is certainly impossible that one of them is not for association, since there is at least one unblemished consecrated animal among animals consecrated for the altar, and with unblemished ones we said above that it is association.

notes.dh: ובעלת מום תחת בעלת מום לאחולי
notes.he: דודאי אתפוסי ליכא למימר דרע ברע לא כתיב דליעביד תמורה:
notes.en: And blemished in place of blemished, to desacralize: for one certainly cannot say [that it is] association, since “bad for bad” is not written [in the verse] so as to effect substitution.

notes.he: בעלת מום תחת בעלת מום לאחולי או דלמא תמימה דחולין תחת בעלת מום דהקדש ובעל מום דחולין תחת תמימה דהקדש תרוייהו לאתפוסי ואתרוייהו לקי - תימה למה האריך כל זה הוה מצי למימר בקיצור בעלת מום תחת בעלת מום לאחולי או דלמא הא נמי לאתפוסי ופירש"י דבעלת מום תחת בעלת מום לא תפיס דאין רע עושה תמורה ברע דדוקא טוב ברע או רע בטוב עושה תמורה אבל רע ברע לא ולא נהירא דזה לא מצינו ועוד דאדרבה משמע לעיל בפ"ק (תמורה דף ט.) דרע ברע תפיס דאמר לעיל א"כ נימא קרא טוב ברע או רע [בו] משמע דרע ברע תפיס מיהו כל השיטה דהכא משמע כפירוש רש"י דבבעיא דלעיל נמי נקט שתי בהמות של חולין תמימות ולא נקט בעל מום ור"י פירש דרע ברע נמי חייל תמורה עליה מיהו יש לנו לומר טפי לאחולי מלאתפוסי דלמה יתפיס מאחר דאינו מעלה אותה דגם זאת אינה ראויה להקרבה:
notes.en: Blemished in place of blemished to desacralize, or perhaps the unblemished non-sacred in place of the blemished consecrated and the blemished non-sacred in place of the unblemished consecrated, both to associate, and he is flogged for both: This is puzzling. Why did it go to such length? It could have said briefly: blemished in place of blemished to desacralize, or perhaps this too is to associate. Rashi explained that blemished in place of blemished does not take hold, since a bad animal does not render substitution with a bad one: only good for bad or bad for good renders substitution, but not bad for bad. But this does not seem right, for we have not found this. Furthermore, on the contrary, it is implied above in the first chapter (Temurah 9a) that bad for bad does take hold, as it said there: If so, let the verse say “good for bad, or bad for it,” implying that bad for bad takes hold. However, the entire passage here implies as Rashi explained, for in the dilemma above, too, it took two unblemished non-sacred animals and did not take a blemished one. And the Ri explained that with bad for bad, too, substitution takes effect; but we have more reason to say desacralization than association, for why would he associate [sanctity with it], since he does not raise it [to anything], as this one too is not fit for sacrifice?

notes.dh: מי אמרינן מה תמימה תחת תמימה קא אמר
notes.he: לאתפוסי תמורה דכיון דשניהן תמימות על איזו שמניח ידו מתפסת בתמורה:
notes.en: Do we say, since he said unblemished in place of unblemished, it is to associate in substitution: for since both are unblemished, whichever one he places his hand on, it is taken hold of in substitution.

notes.he: תחת בעל מום דהקדש:
notes.en: And the blemished [non-sacred animal] in place of the blemished consecrated animal.

messages.text: Or perhaps, he intended that the unblemished non-sacred animal should be consecrated as a substitute in place of the blemished consecrated animal, and the blemished non-sacred animal should be consecrated as a substitute in place of the unblemished consecrated animal, and since he intended to perform substitution in both cases he is flogged for both pairings.

notes.dh: או דלמא תמימה דחולין תחת בעלת מום כו'
notes.he: ואף על גב דפשיט לעיל דלא שביק היתירא ועביד איסורא איכא למיבעי הכא הואיל ואי אפשר דלא עביד איסורא בחדא איכא למימר כי היכי דבהא עביד איסורא בהא נמי לא איכפת ליה ודאי אתפוסי הוא:
notes.en: Or perhaps the unblemished non-sacred in place of the blemished, etc.: even though it was resolved above that one does not abandon the permitted way and perform the prohibited, there is room to ask here. Since it is impossible that he did not perform a prohibition with one of them, one may say: just as he performs a prohibition with this one, he does not mind with that one too, and it is certainly association.

notes.he: דחולין תחת תמימה דהקדש דהיינו טוב ברע או רע בטוב ואתרוייהו לקי:
notes.en: And the blemished non-sacred animal in place of the unblemished consecrated animal, which is good for bad or bad for good, and he is flogged for both.

messages.text: And if you say that anywhere that there exists both a permitted and a prohibited manner to perform an action, one does not perform the prohibition, this would resolve the previous dilemma, as his intention must have been to desacralize the blemished consecrated animal, and therefore he is not flogged two sets of lashes.

notes.he: ואת"ל היכא דאיכא קצת למיעבד בהיתירא לא עבד כולה באיסורא ולאחולי הוא ולא לקי אלא חדא:
notes.en: And if you say: where there is some [way] to act in a permitted manner, he does not do all of it in a prohibited manner, and it is to desacralize, and he is flogged only once.

messages.text: One can raise the following dilemma: In a case where there were three sacrificial animals before him, one of which was blemished while the other two were unblemished, and three non-sacred animals, all of which were unblemished, and he said: These animals are hereby in place of [taḥat] those animals, what is the halakha?

notes.he: דאף על גב דפשיטנא דלא שביק היתירא ועביד איסורא איכא הכא למיבעי דאיכא למימר זיל בתר רובא כיון דע"כ תרתי לאתפוסי דהשתים דהקדש תמימות וליכא אחולי בהו שלישית נמי אתפוסי הוא:
notes.en: If there were three animals before him, etc.: even though I resolved that one does not abandon the permitted way and perform the prohibited, there is room to ask here, for one may say: go after the majority. Since two are perforce for association, as the two consecrated ones are unblemished and desacralization does not apply to them, the third too is association.

messages.text: Do we say that since he intended for the unblemished non-sacred animals to be consecrated as substitutes in place of the unblemished consecrated animals, i.e., to associate their sanctity, so too he intended to consecrate the unblemished non-sacred animal as a substitute in place of the blemished consecrated animal, i.e., to associate its sanctity, and he therefore is flogged three sets of lashes?
messages.quote: three sacrificial animals before him, one of which was blemished

notes.dh: היו לפניו ג' בהמות של קודש ואחת מהן בעלת מום כו'
notes.he: מי אמרי' מתמימה תחת תמימה לאתפוסי:
notes.en: If there were before him three consecrated animals and one of them blemished, etc.: Do we say, from [the fact that] unblemished in place of unblemished is to associate,

notes.dh: תמימה דחולין נמי תחת בעל מום
notes.he: דקודש לאיתפוסי דאזלינן בתר רובה:
notes.en: the unblemished non-sacred one too [stands] in place of the blemished consecrated one, to associate, for we follow the majority?

messages.text: Or perhaps, here too one applies the principle that anywhere that there exists both a permitted and a prohibited manner to perform an action, a person does not perform the prohibition. If so, his intention with regard to this latter blemished consecrated animal was to desacralize it, and therefore he is not flogged for transferring its sanctity to a substitute.

And if you say that here too, since this man has not yet been established as one who regularly transgresses a prohibition, until he has done so three times, therefore it is assumed that he does not cast aside the permitted manner and perform the prohibition,

notes.he: דבשלשה זימנין הויא חזקה תרי זימני לא הוי חזקה לשון ירושלמי בעי אביי (כו') או דלמא תמימה תחת תמימה דאתפוסי דחזיא להקרבה אבל תמימה תחת בעלת מום דבעלת מום דהקדש לא (הוי') חזיא להקרבה לאחולי איכוון כיון דבעא למימר חדא לאתפוסי כו' כלומר דאילו הוה בדעתיה לאתפוסי חדא ולאחולי חדא הוה קאמר בהדיא הך לאתפוסי והך לאחולי כי הדדי כלומר שתיהן עשאן שוות הואיל ולא פירש על שתיהן הניח ידו ושתיהן תמורה דהא איבעי ליה לאתנוחי ידיה על בעלת מום דקדש אי הוה בדעתיה לאחוליה אלא אי הוה לפניו (כו') מדהני תרתי בהמות לאתפוסי דודאי מתפיס הנך תרתי דחולין בההיא דקדש דממירין שנים באחד דהא כיון דתמימה דקדש ליכא למימר לאחולי אההיא בעלת מום נמי לאתפוסי ולקי שלשה מלקיות או דלמא ההיא בעלת מום דקדש לאחולי והאי דלא אתנח ידיה על ההיא דבעלת מום שהניח ידו על חולין דכיון דלאחולי הוה בעי הוה ליה לאנוחי אבעלת מום דקדש. הא דנקט כל ההיא דבעלת מום קמ"ל דאי הוה מנח ידיה על התמימה של קדש שעם הבעלת מום הוה מהני נמי כאילו אנחה על בעלת מום גופה והא אמרי' בההיא דבת אחולי היא דלאחולי איכוון ובתמימה לאתפוסי דאע"ג דאנח ידיה עליה הואיל וליכא למימר אחולי בה בדידה. רמי רמויי כגון דהויין ג' בהמות של קדש ואחת בעלת מום ושלשה בהמות של חולין תמימות והעמידן בשתי שורות זו כנגד זו והאי רמי כמו איתרמי שכוונם זו מול זו ואנח ידיה על הנך דחולין ואמר אלו תחת אלו מי אמרינן כיון דרמי חדא לקביל חדא להכי פלגינהו דלא בעי לשוויי לבעל מום כי הני דהיינו לאתפוסי אלא לאחולי או דלמא בתר דבורא דידיה אזלינן והרי הניח ידו על החול ולאתפוסי איכוון. לישנא אחרינא או דלמא בתר רובא אזלינן וכיון דרובא לאתפוסי איהו נמי לאתפוסי:
notes.en: The man has not been established: for three times make a presumption [ḥazaka]; twice is not a presumption. [Rashi now records a different version of the passage, which he calls] the Jerusalem version: Abaye raised a dilemma, etc. Or perhaps unblemished in place of unblemished is for association, since [the consecrated animal] is fit for sacrifice; but unblemished in place of blemished, since the blemished consecrated animal is not fit for sacrifice, he intended to desacralize. Since he wished to say one for association, etc.: that is, had it been in his mind to associate one and to desacralize one, he would have said explicitly: this one to associate and this one to desacralize. “Alike”: that is, he made both of them equal, since he did not specify; he placed his hand on both [non-sacred animals], and both are substitutes, for had it been in his mind to desacralize it he should have placed his hand on the blemished consecrated animal. Rather, if there were before him, etc.: since these two animals are for association, for he certainly associates these two non-sacred animals with that consecrated one, as one may substitute two for one, and since the consecrated one is unblemished one cannot say [it is] to desacralize, that blemished one too is for association, and he is flogged three sets of lashes. Or perhaps that blemished consecrated animal is for desacralization, and [as for] the fact that he did not place his hand on that blemished one but placed his hand on the non-sacred ones [it is no proof], for since he wished to desacralize, he should have placed it on the blemished consecrated animal. The reason it states “that whole blemished one” is to teach us that had he placed his hand on the unblemished consecrated animal that is with the blemished one, it would also be effective, as though he had placed it on the blemished one itself; and we say of that one, which can be desacralized, that he intended to desacralize, and of the unblemished one, to associate, even though he placed his hand on it, since desacralization cannot be said of it itself. Rami ramuyei [he set them opposite each other]: for example, there were three consecrated animals, one of them blemished, and three unblemished non-sacred animals, and he set them in two rows, one opposite the other (and this rami is like “it happened,” that he aligned them one opposite the other), and he placed his hand on the non-sacred ones and said: These are in place of those. Do we say that since he set one opposite one, he divided them for this reason, that he did not wish to treat the blemished one like these, that is, for association, but rather for desacralization? Or perhaps we follow his own words, and he placed his hand on the non-sacred ones and intended to associate. Another version: Or perhaps we follow the majority, and since the majority are for association, it too is for association.

notes.dh: או דלמא הכא נמי אמרי' כל היכא כו'
notes.he: כיון דאכתי גברא לא אתחזק תלתא זימני באיסורי למעבד תמורה אמרינן לא שביק התירא אלא לאחולי הוא:
notes.en: Or perhaps here too we say: wherever, etc. Since the man has not yet been established three times in transgressing by performing substitution, we say that he does not abandon the permitted way, and it is to desacralize.

messages.text: If there were four sacrificial animals standing before him, one of which was blemished and the other three were unblemished, and four non-sacred animals, all of which were unblemished, and he said: These animals are hereby in place of [taḥat] those animals, what is the halakha?

notes.dh: בעי רב אשי היו לפניו כו'
notes.he: ל"א בעי אביי היו לפניו כו' או דלמא תמימה תחת תמימה לאיתפוסי דחזיא תמימה דקודש להקרבה הלכך תפסה תמורה אבל תמימה תחת בעל מום של קודש דלא הויא בעלת מום לא תפסה תמורה אלא לאחולי הוא:
notes.en: Rav Ashi raises a dilemma: If there were before him, etc. Another version: Abaye raises a dilemma: If there were before him, etc. Or perhaps unblemished in place of unblemished is to associate, since the unblemished consecrated animal is fit for sacrifice, and therefore substitution takes hold; but unblemished in place of the blemished consecrated animal, since the blemished one is not [fit], substitution does not take hold, and it is to desacralize.

messages.text: Here, since it is certain that he intended for three unblemished non-sacred animals to be consecrated as substitutes in place of the three unblemished consecrated animals, this man has been established as one who regularly transgresses a prohibition. Therefore, it is assumed that he also intended for one of the unblemished non-sacred animals to be consecrated as a substitute in place of the blemished consecrated animal, which means he is liable to be flogged four sets of lashes for the four substitutions.
messages.quote: four sacrificial animals standing before him, one of which was blemished

notes.he: ואת"ל הכא כיון דבעי למימר בפירוש חדא לאיתפוסי וחדא לאחולי ולא אמר תרוייהו תפסו דתרויהון כי הדדי אנח ידיה על הנהו דחולין דאי לאחולי איתבעי ליה לאתנוחי ידיה על ההיא בעלת מום כדאמרינן לעיל הניח ידו על הקודש חולין מדלא אתנח ידיה עלה אלא על תמימה דחולין ש"מ תרוייהו תפסן:
notes.en: And if you say: here, since he should have said explicitly “one to associate and one to desacralize” and did not say so, both take hold, for he placed his hand on both of those non-sacred animals alike. For if [he meant] to desacralize, he should have placed his hand on that blemished one, as we said above: [if] he placed his hand on the consecrated animal, it is non-sacred. Since he did not place his hand on it, but on the unblemished non-sacred one, learn from this that both take hold.

messages.text: Or perhaps, even though in this case he has been established as one who transgresses the prohibition, nevertheless even such a person does not cast aside the permitted manner and perform the prohibition. And if so, his intention with regard to this latter blemished animal was to desacralize it.

notes.he: אלא היו לפניו ב' בהמות של קודש ואחת מהן בעלת מום ושלש בהמות תמימות [של חול] והניח ידו על בהמה תמימה של חול ואמר הרי אלו תחת אלו והכא המיר ב' תמימות של חולין בתמימית אחת של קודש וכדתנן בפ"ק ממירין אחד בשנים כו':
notes.en: Rather, if there were before him two consecrated animals, one of them blemished, and three unblemished [non-sacred] animals, and he placed his hand on an unblemished non-sacred animal and said: These are hereby in place of those. Here he substituted two unblemished non-sacred animals for one unblemished consecrated animal, as we learned in the first chapter: One may substitute one for two, etc.

notes.he: מי אמרינן מדהני תרתין בהמה תמימה של חולין לאתפוסי בההיא תמימה דקודש ההיא תמימה שלישית של חול לאתפוסי תחת בעלת מום דקודש או דלמא לאחולי הוא והדין דלא אתנח ידיה על ההיא תמימה דקודש דבהדי בעלת מום ולא על בעלת מום נמי דהכי הוה דיניה אי הוה לאחולי האי דלא אתנח משום דקסבר רובה עדיף מוטב להניח על הרוב שלש ולא על השתים אבל מכל מקום דעתו לאחולי תיבעי. [רמויי רמי] חדא להדי חדא כלומר אם חיבר כל אחת של הקדש כנגד אחת של חולין והנהו חולין כולן תמימין וחדא דהקדש בעלת מום ואמר אלו תחת אלו מאי מי אמרינן כיון דרמי חדא להדי חדא מעשיו מוכיחין דתמימה כנגד תמימה לאתפוסי ובעל מום כנגד תמימה לאחולי או דלמא לא משגיחינן ארמויי אלא בתר דבורא אזלינן דאמר הרי אלו תחת אלו והאי משמע נמי דאמר אתמימה דחולין וליהוו כולהו לאיתפוסי:
notes.en: Do we say: since these two unblemished non-sacred animals are to associate with that unblemished consecrated one, the third unblemished non-sacred one is [also] to associate, in place of the blemished consecrated one? Or perhaps it is to desacralize; and as for his not placing his hand on that unblemished consecrated one that is with the blemished one, nor on the blemished one, as the rule would have been had it been to desacralize, he did not place it there because he holds that the majority is preferable: better to place it on the majority, the three, and not on the two. But in any case his intention was to desacralize. Let it stand [unresolved]. [Rami ramuyei,] one opposite one: that is, if he set each consecrated animal opposite a non-sacred one, and those non-sacred ones are all unblemished and one consecrated animal is blemished, and he said: These are in place of those, what [is the halakha]? Do we say that since he set one opposite one, his actions prove that unblemished opposite unblemished is to associate and blemished opposite unblemished is to desacralize? Or perhaps we pay no attention to how he set them, but follow his words, for he said: These are in place of those, and this also implies that he said it about the unblemished non-sacred ones, and all of them are to associate?

notes.he: ל"א או דלמא בתר רובה אזלינן דהנהו דחולין הוו רובה ואהנהו אנח ידיה וליהויין כולהו לאיתפוסי תבעי:
notes.en: Another version: Or perhaps we follow the majority, for those non-sacred animals are the majority and on them he placed his hand, and all of them are to associate. Let it stand [unresolved].

messages.text: All of these dilemmas shall stand unresolved.

messages.caption: “These are hereby in place of those”: the four cases, from Abaye’s dilemma to Rav Ashi’s, and the two ways each might be read.

messages.text: Rashi and Rabbeinu Gershom also record another version of these dilemmas, not in our printed text, which asks where he placed his hand and what happens if he set each consecrated animal opposite a non-sacred one; see their notes on the last few messages.

If the consecrated animal was blemished, and he said: This consecrated animal is desacralized, with its sanctity transferred to that non-sacred animal, the consecrated animal is desacralized. The owner is required to conduct an appraisal to ascertain the relative value of the two animals, and if the consecrated animal was worth more than the non-sacred animal, he must pay the difference to the Temple treasury.

notes.he: משום דכי אמר בלשון תמורה אינו יוצא לחולין אלא הוא ותמורתו קודש אבל כשאמר הרי זו מחוללת שלא אמר בלשון תמורה:
notes.en: It is desacralized by Torah law: because when he says it in the language of substitution it does not go out to non-sacred status, but both it and its substitute are sacred; but when he said: This is hereby desacralized, he did not speak in the language of substitution.

messages.text: The consecrated animal is desacralized by Torah law even if the consecrated animal was worth one hundred dinars and the non-sacred animal was worth only one peruta. But by rabbinic law, the owner is required to conduct an appraisal to ascertain the relative value of the two animals and to pay the difference to the Temple treasury, so that the Temple treasury not suffer a loss.

notes.he: דאמרינן בפ' המנחות והנסכים (מנחות קא.) ואם כל בהמה טמאה בבעלי מומין שנפדו הכתוב מדבר:
notes.en: It is desacralized by Torah law: as we say in the chapter HaMenaḥot VehaNesakhim (Menaḥot 101a): “And if it be any impure animal” (Leviticus 27:11): the verse speaks of blemished animals that were redeemed.

notes.he: דמה"ת אין אונאה להקדש דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:י״ד) אל תונו איש את אחיו ולא הקדש:
notes.en: By rabbinic law: for by Torah law there is no exploitation for consecrated property, as it is written: “You shall not wrong one another [literally: a man his brother]” (Leviticus 25:14), and not consecrated property.

notes.he: כפסולי המוקדשין דניכרין וצריך לעשות לו דמים כדאמרן לעיל מדבריהן של חכמים שדברי תורה אין אונאה להקדשות דעמיתו כתיב למעוטי דהקדש במאי פליגי אי נימא אאונאה אדין אונאה. ל"א קאמר בפירוש דטעו בשתות דהיינו דין אונאה דחייב להחזיר לו בהא נימא ריש לקיש דבר תורה והתנן כו':
notes.en: It is desacralized by Torah law, like disqualified consecrated animals that are redeemed; and he must conduct an appraisal, as we said above, by the words of the Sages, for by Torah law consecrated property is not subject to exploitation, as “his fellow” is written, to exclude consecrated property. With regard to what do they disagree? If we say with regard to exploitation, the law of exploitation. Another version says explicitly: that they erred by one-sixth, which is the law of exploitation, where he is obligated to return it to him; in this case would Reish Lakish say it is by Torah law? But didn’t we learn, etc.

messages.text: Even the requirement to conduct an appraisal, to ascertain the relative value of the two animals and to pay the difference to the Temple treasury, applies by Torah law.

notes.dh: אף צריך לעשות לו דמים דבר תורה
notes.he: רב חסדא מפרש לה לקמן:
notes.en: Even required to conduct an appraisal by Torah law: Rav Ḥisda explains it below.

notes.dh: אף צריך לעשות דמים דבר תורה
notes.he: ולא יצא לחולין עד שיעשהו דמים והכי פירושא דמתני' יצא לחולין וצריך לעשותו דמים כלומר יצא לחולין כשיעשהו דמים והא דאיצטריך למיתני יצא לחולין משום דתנא לעיל מינה לישני דלא נפקי לחולין אלא נתפסין בתמורה וזה וזה קדושים תנא נמי לישנא דאחולי:
notes.en: Even required to conduct an appraisal by Torah law: and it does not go out to non-sacred status until he conducts the appraisal. This is the meaning of the mishna, “it is desacralized and he must conduct an appraisal”: that is, it is desacralized when he conducts the appraisal. The reason it needed to teach “it is desacralized” is that it taught just before it expressions by which [the animals] do not go out to non-sacred status but are taken hold of in substitution, so that both this and that are sacred; so it also taught an expression of desacralization.

messages.text: What are we dealing with here, i.e., what is the case that is subject to the disagreement between Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish? If we say that they disagree in a case where the difference in value between the two animals was exactly one-sixth, which is the difference in value that constitutes exploitation by Torah law, and the halakha is that such a transaction is valid but one must return the difference in value, would Reish Lakish say that even in such a case the requirement to conduct an appraisal to ascertain the relative value of the two animals applies by Torah law?
messages.quote: Even the requirement to conduct an appraisal … applies by Torah law

notes.he: דלא נתאנה אלא שתות:
notes.en: If we say regarding exploitation: that he was wronged by only one-sixth.

messages.text: But didn’t we learn in a mishna (Bava Metzia 56a):
These are matters that, even if the disparity between the value and the payment is one-sixth, are not subject to the halakhot of exploitation: Slaves, documents, lands, and consecrated property.

Since consecrated property is not subject to the halakhot of exploitation, why would Reish Lakish say that one must repay the difference in value between the two animals to the Temple treasury by Torah law?

Rather, Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish disagree with regard to a case of nullification of a transaction, i.e., where the difference in value between the two animals was greater than one-sixth. Would Rabbi Yoḥanan say in such a case that one is required to conduct an appraisal to ascertain the relative value of the two animals by rabbinic law?
messages.quote: But by rabbinic law, the owner is required to conduct an appraisal

notes.he: שנתאנה יותר משתות:
notes.en: Nullification of a transaction: that he was wronged by more than one-sixth.

notes.he: ואלא דטעו בכדי ביטול מקח ביותר משתות בהא נימא ר' יוחנן מדבריהם ולא דברי תורה הא איתמר ר' יונה אמר אהקדשות האי דבעי למימר לקמיה דביטול מקח יש להן דבר תורה:
notes.en: Rather, where they erred by the measure of nullification of a transaction, more than one-sixth: in this case would Rabbi Yoḥanan say it is by rabbinic law and not by Torah law? But it was stated: Rabbi Yona said with regard to consecrated property this which it goes on to say below, that they are subject to nullification of a transaction by Torah law.

messages.text: But didn’t Rabbi Yirmeya say this ruling with regard to non-sacred lands, and Rabbi Yona said it with regard to consecrated property, and both of them said it in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:

notes.he: משמיה דר' יוחנן אקרקע דחולין ורבי יונה אמר משמיה דר' יוחנן אהקדש:
notes.en: But didn’t Rabbi Yirmeya say: in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan, with regard to non-sacred land; and Rabbi Yona said [it] in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan with regard to consecrated property.

messages.alt: as reported by Rabbi Yirmeya and Rabbi Yona
messages.text: They are not subject to the halakhot of exploitation, in the case of a disparity of one-sixth. But they are subject to nullification of a transaction, in the case of a greater disparity.

notes.dh: אונאה אין להן ביטול מקח יש להן
notes.he: שאם נתאנה יותר משתות חוזר. לרבי יונה קשיא דר' יוחנן אדר' יוחנן:
notes.en: They are not subject to exploitation, but they are subject to nullification of a transaction: that if he was wronged by more than one-sixth, he may retract. According to Rabbi Yona, [one statement of] Rabbi Yoḥanan contradicts [another statement of] Rabbi Yoḥanan.

notes.he: יש להן בטול מקח ותרוייהו משמיה דרבי יוחנן אמרי בטול מקח יש להן. דבר תורה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yirmeya said with regard to land that they are subject to nullification of a transaction, and both said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: they are subject to nullification of a transaction, by Torah law.

messages.text: If so, according to the opinion of Rabbi Yona, Rabbi Yoḥanan maintains that when the disparity between the value and the payment is greater than one-sixth, the transaction is nullified by Torah law. But in that case, why would Rabbi Yoḥanan rule here that only by rabbinic law is he required to calculate the difference and pay its value?

Actually, they disagree in a case of nullification of a transaction, i.e., more than one-sixth, and one should reverse attribution of the opinions; the opinion previously attributed to Rabbi Yoḥanan is actually that of Reish Lakish, and the opinion attributed to Reish Lakish is the ruling of Rabbi Yoḥanan.

notes.he: ר' יוחנן אמר צריך לעשות דמים דבר תורה ור"ש בן לקיש אמר מדבריהם:
notes.en: Reverse: Rabbi Yoḥanan said that one is required to conduct an appraisal by Torah law, and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said by rabbinic law.

notes.he: דר' יוחנן דאמר מדבריהם תריץ ליה כריש לקיש ודריש לקיש כר' יוחנן ולא קשיא לך:
notes.en: And reverse: Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said by rabbinic law, explain him as Reish Lakish, and Reish Lakish as Rabbi Yoḥanan, and it is not difficult for you.

messages.text: But how can you say that one should reverse the attribution of the opinions of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish? This works out well according to the one who says that Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that consecrated property is not subject to the halakhot of exploitation if the disparity between the value and the payment is one-sixth, but it is subject to nullification of the transaction if the disparity between the value and the payment is greater than one-sixth. According to this opinion, that of Rabbi Yona, it is apparent all the more so that lands are subject to nullification if the disparity is greater than one-sixth.
messages.quote: one should reverse attribution of the opinions

notes.he: לרבי יונה דאמר אהקדשות אמר ר' יוחנן דיש להן ביטול מקח ואע"ג דכתיב אחיו וכ"ש אקרקעות ניחא מאי דאפכת לה:
notes.en: This works out well: according to Rabbi Yona, who said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said with regard to consecrated property that it is subject to nullification of a transaction, even though “his brother” is written, and all the more so with regard to lands, what you reversed works out well.

messages.text: But according to the one who said that Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that only lands are subject to nullification if the disparity is greater than one-sixth, but with regard to consecrated property there is no nullification of a transaction, i.e., Rabbi Yirmeya, how can he reverse attribution of that opinion, and claim that Rabbi Yoḥanan maintains that he is required to pay the difference in value by Torah law?

notes.he: אי אפכת לה קשיא דר' יוחנן אדר' יוחנן:
notes.en: But according to Rabbi Yirmeya: if you reverse it, [one statement of] Rabbi Yoḥanan contradicts [another statement of] Rabbi Yoḥanan.

notes.he: הניחא למ"ד לר' יוחנן דאמר דהקדש יש להן ביטול מקח וכ"ש אקרקע איצטריך למימר איפוך אלא לר' ירמיה אקרקע יש להן ביטול מקח ולא אהקדש היכי אפיך לה:
notes.en: But can you say reverse? This works out well according to the one who says that Rabbi Yoḥanan said that consecrated property is subject to nullification of a transaction, and all the more so with regard to land; it was necessary to say reverse. But according to Rabbi Yirmeya, land is subject to nullification of a transaction and not consecrated property; how can he reverse it?

messages.text: According to my opinion, do not reverse attribution of the opinions of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish. In other words, Rabbi Yoḥanan maintains that he is required to pay the difference in value by rabbinic law.

notes.dh: אמר לך ר' ירמיה לא תיפוך
notes.he: דודאי הכי הוא כדאמר ברישא ורבי יונה מתרץ לטעמיה ומפיך לה:
notes.en: Rabbi Yirmeya could say to you: Do not reverse: [Rashi’s text reads “Rabbi Yirmeya could say to you,” where ours reads “Rabbi Yirmeya said.”] For it certainly is as was said at first, and Rabbi Yona answers according to his own reasoning and reverses it.

notes.he: ור' יוחנן מדבריהם קאמר יש להן ביטול מקח ולא מדאורייתא לדברי רבי ירמיה:
notes.en: Rather, do not reverse: and Rabbi Yoḥanan says that they are subject to nullification of a transaction by rabbinic law and not by Torah law, according to the words of Rabbi Yirmeya.

messages.text: This is consistent with Rabbi Yirmeya’s ruling that Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that there is no nullification of a transaction in the case of consecrated property. Only Rabbi Yona would reverse attribution of the opinions of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish in order for Rabbi Yoḥanan’s opinion to be consistent with his statement, as cited by Rabbi Yona, that there is nullification of a transaction in the case of consecrated property.

It has been established that Rabbi Yona maintains that according to Rabbi Yoḥanan consecrated property is subject to nullification of a transaction, whereas Rabbi Yirmeya disputes that claim. Shall we say that they disagree with regard to a statement of Shmuel, as Shmuel said:

notes.he: ר' יונה ור' ירמיה בדשמואל דאמר שמואל הקדש שוה מנה שחיללו על שוה פרוטה מחולל:
notes.en: Shall we say that they disagree: Rabbi Yona and Rabbi Yirmeya, with regard to Shmuel’s [statement], as Shmuel said: Consecrated property worth a maneh that one desacralized onto a peruta’s worth is desacralized.

messages.text: Consecrated property worth one hundred dinars [maneh] that one desacralized, with its sanctity transferred to a coin worth one peruta, is desacralized.

Since consecrated property is not subject to nullification of a transaction, it is desacralized by coins worth any sum. The suggestion is that Rabbi Yona is not of the opinion that the halakha follows the ruling of Shmuel, and Rabbi Yirmeya is of the opinion that the halakha follows the ruling of Shmuel.
messages.quote: Consecrated property worth one hundred dinars that one desacralized … is desacralized

notes.he: דקסבר בטול מקח יש להן והאי שחיללו על פרוטה היינו טפי מבטול מקח ור' ירמיה אית ליה:
notes.en: That Rabbi Yona does not hold in accordance with Shmuel: for he holds that they are subject to nullification of a transaction, and this one, who desacralized it onto a peruta, [is] more than nullification of a transaction. And Rabbi Yirmeya does hold [in accordance with Shmuel].

messages.text: No; both this Sage and that Sage are of the opinion that the halakha follows the ruling of Shmuel. The difference between them is that Rabbi Yona maintains that when Shmuel stated his halakha, he was referring to consecrated property that one desacralized after the fact, but he did not say that one may do so ab initio; and Rabbi Yirmeya maintains that Shmuel rules that it is permitted to desacralize consecrated property with coins worth any sum, even ab initio.

notes.dh: לא בין למר בין למר אית להו דשמואל
notes.he: ואי כדקמכוון לאחולי ודאי מיתחיל כלומר אם היה בדעתו לאנות ההקדש ולחלל בדמים פחותין ודאי מיתחיל אבל להכי אמר ר"ל צריך לעשות דמים דבר תורה משום דאיהו לא מיכווין לחללו בדמים פחותין אלא סבור שיהו החולין שוין את דמי ההקדש ור' יוחנן סבר בכך מתכוין לחללו:
notes.en: No, both this Sage and that Sage hold in accordance with Shmuel: and if he intends to desacralize it [for less], it is certainly desacralized; that is, if it was in his mind to wrong the consecrated property and desacralize it for less money, it is certainly desacralized. But Reish Lakish said that one is required to conduct an appraisal by Torah law for this reason: because he did not intend to desacralize it for less money, but thought that the non-sacred animal was worth the value of the consecrated one; and Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that even so he intends to desacralize it.

notes.dh: בין למר בין למר אית ליה דשמואל כו'
notes.he: פרש"י ואי בדקא מיכוון לאחולי ודאי מיתחיל כלומר אם היה בדעתו לאנות ההקדש ולחללו בדמים פחותים ודאי מיתחיל אבל להכי אמר ר' שמעון בן לקיש צריך לעשות לו דמים דבר תורה משום דלאו איהו קמיכוין לחללו בדמים פחותים אלא סבר הוא שיהו החולין שוין דמי ההקדש ורבי יוחנן סבר בכך ודאי מתכוין לחללו עכ"ל וכן נפרש משמעות הלשון כי אמר שמואל דיעבד כלו' דבר שאינו מותר לעשותו לכתחלה אלא דיעבד וכגון שחיללו במתכוין בפחות משויין אבל לכתחלה כלומר דבר שמותר לכתחלה כמו שלא נתכוין לחללו על פחות משוויו אלא כסבור היה החולין שוין דמי ההקדש ונמצא שטעה לא אמר שמואל בכך שיחול ההקדש עליו ורבי ירמיה סבר אפילו לכתחלה כלומר דבר המותר לכתחלה כגון שלא נתכוין להפחותו משויו אמר שמואל דמחולל אבל אין לפרש כדמשמע לפום ריהטא כי אמר שמואל דמחולל היינו דיעבד אבל לכתחלה לא דא"כ הא דאמר [משמיה] (משמע) דר' יוחנן בטול מקח יש להן היינו לכתחלה והיכי קאמר דאונאה אין להן וכי מותר להונות ההקדש לכתחלה ועוד היכי קאמר רבי ירמיה אפילו לכתחלה אמר שמואל דמותר לחלל שוה מנה על שוה פרוטה ועוד מחולל דאמר שמואל משמע דיעבד ועוד דאמר פ"ק דסנהדרין (דף יד:) דבעינן לחלל ההקדש תשעה ישראל וכהן אחד ויליף לה התם מקראי לכך צריך לפרש כדפי' רש"י:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot quotes Rashi’s explanation [that if he meant to wrong the Temple and desacralize the property for less, it is certainly desacralized, while Reish Lakish requires an appraisal by Torah law because the owner thought the non-sacred animal was worth as much as the consecrated one, and Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that even so he means to desacralize it]. Accordingly they explain the wording: “When Shmuel stated it, after the fact” means a case that is permitted not ab initio but only after the fact, where he intentionally desacralized it for less than its value; “but not ab initio” means a case that is permitted ab initio, where he did not intend to lower its value but thought the non-sacred was worth as much as the consecrated and erred, and there Shmuel did not say that the sanctity transfers. Rabbi Yirmeya holds that Shmuel said it is desacralized even in that case. One cannot explain at face value that Shmuel said it is desacralized after the fact but not that one may do so ab initio: for then Rabbi Yoḥanan’s statement that they are not subject to exploitation but are subject to nullification would be speaking ab initio, and is one permitted to wrong consecrated property ab initio? Further, how could Rabbi Yirmeya say that Shmuel permits desacralizing property worth a maneh on a peruta’s worth even ab initio? Further, Shmuel’s word “is desacralized” itself implies after the fact. And further, the first chapter of Sanhedrin (14b) says that redeeming consecrated property requires nine Israelites and one priest, derived there from verses. Therefore one must explain as Rashi did. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: Actually, do not reverse the attribution of their respective opinions. In fact, they disagree with regard to a disparity of one-sixth, and Reish Lakish holds that one is required to pay the difference value by Torah law.
messages.lead: If you wish, say instead, with regard to the dispute between Reish Lakish and Rabbi Yoḥanan:

notes.dh: ואיבעית אימא אפילו לר' יונה לא תיפוך
notes.he: להא דר יוחנן ור"ל ואאונאה קיימי ובביטול מקח לא איירו כלל ודקא קשיא לך לריש לקיש ממתני' דאלו דברים לא קשיא דההיא מתרץ לה ריש לקיש כדרב חסדא דאפילו פחות משתות חוזר וה"ק קרא איש את אחיו הוא דבשיעור שתות משלם פחות משתות לא משלם הא הקדש אפי' פחות מכדי אונאה חוזר והיינו דבר תורה דקאמר ר"ל לעיל ורבי יוחנן מוקי ליה כמשמעותיה אבל בביטול מקח לא איירי כלל ר"י ולא תיקשי לא לרבי יוחנן ולא לרבי ירמיה:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: even according to Rabbi Yona, do not reverse this [dispute] of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish. They are dealing with exploitation, and did not speak of nullification of a transaction at all. And as for the difficulty for Reish Lakish from the mishna “These are matters,” it is not difficult, for Reish Lakish explains it in accordance with Rav Ḥisda: that even [a disparity of] less than one-sixth is returned. This is what the verse “a man [to] his brother” is saying: it is [there] that he pays a disparity of one-sixth, and less than one-sixth he does not pay; but with consecrated property, even less than the measure of exploitation is returned. And this is the “by Torah law” that Reish Lakish said above. And Rabbi Yoḥanan understands [the mishna] according to its plain meaning. But Rabbi Yoḥanan did not speak of nullification of a transaction at all, and there is no difficulty, either for Rabbi Yoḥanan or for Rabbi Yirmeya.

messages.text: And as for that which poses a difficulty for you with regard to the opinion of Reish Lakish, that it is taught in the mishna: These are matters that are not subject to the halakhot of exploitation: Slaves, documents, lands, and consecrated property, which indicates that one is required to pay the difference in value by rabbinic law, that mishna should be understood in accordance with the explanation of Rav Ḥisda.
messages.quote: These are matters that … are not subject to the halakhot of exploitation

notes.he: כדאמר מעיקרא דאאונאה פליגי אשתות ולא תיפוך ודקא קשיא לריש לקיש ואלו דברים שאין להם אונאה הקדש סבר לה דאין להן אונאה כדרב חסדא דאפילו פחות מכדי אונאה חוזר ל"א במאי קמפלגי ר' יוחנן וריש לקיש בדשמואל לר' יוחנן דאמר אחד זו ואחד זו דבר תורה לית ליה דשמואל כדמתרצינן איפוך ואב"א אפילו רב אית ליה דשמואל ואמר לך רב אי דקא מכוין לכתחלה לאחולי בכך בשוה פרוטה [מתחלה שפיר] (מיתחיל) אלא שאני הכא במתני' באומר זו מחולל על זו דלא קא מכוין לאחולי בפרוטה הלכך קאמר וצריך לעשות לו דמים דבר תורה:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: Actually, as was said at first, that they disagree with regard to exploitation, a disparity of one-sixth, and do not reverse. As for what is difficult for Reish Lakish, “These are matters that are not subject to exploitation: consecrated property,” he holds that they are not subject to exploitation as Rav Ḥisda explains, that even less than the measure of exploitation is returned. Another version: With regard to what do Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish disagree? With regard to Shmuel’s [statement]. According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said both this and that are by Torah law, he does not hold in accordance with Shmuel, as we answered “reverse.” And if you wish, say: even Rav [the text reads “Rav,” perhaps for Reish Lakish] holds in accordance with Shmuel, and he could say to you: if he intends ab initio to desacralize it thus, onto a peruta’s worth, it is properly desacralized; but here in the mishna it is different, with one who says “This is desacralized onto this,” who does not intend to desacralize it for a peruta. Therefore it says that he must conduct an appraisal by Torah law.

notes.he: ואב"א דכ"ע לית להו דשמואל ופליגי בכדי אונאה כו':
notes.en: And if you wish, say: no one holds in accordance with Shmuel, and they disagree with regard to the measure of exploitation, etc.

messages.text: What is the meaning of the phrase: Are not subject to the halakhot of exploitation? This means that they are not subject to the standard principles of exploitation at all; rather, more stringent halakhot apply in these cases. As, even if the disparity is less than the measure of exploitation, i.e., less than one-sixth, one may renege on the transaction, and in the case of consecrated property he is required to pay the value of the disparity.

messages.caption: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish on paying the Temple the difference: the readings the Gemara tries, and what each must answer.

messages.text: The Sages said that one must pay the value of the disparity to the Temple treasury only if the value of the consecrated property was initially assessed by only two people and afterward three other people determined that the consecrated property was worth more. But in a case where the value of the consecrated property was initially assessed by three people, as required by halakha, and that amount was paid to the Temple treasury, even if afterward one hundred people came and assessed the value of the consecrated property at a higher value, one need not return the disparity of value to the Temple treasury.
messages.lead: § With regard to a case in which there was a disparity between the assessed value of property and its actual value, where one must pay the difference to the Temple treasury:

notes.he: דמשלם לו הדיוט להקדש כל האונאה אלא דשמוה בי תרי ברישא וטעו ותו הדרי תלתא ושיימוה להקדש טפי:
notes.en: They said only: that a layman pays the consecrated property the entire disparity, only where two assessed it at first and erred, and then three returned and assessed it higher for the consecrated property.

notes.he: מעיקרא אפילו הדור בי מאה ואמרי' דקמא טעו לא הדרא שומא:
notes.en: But where three assessed it: at first, even if a hundred come back and say that the first ones erred, the assessment is not reversed.

notes.dh: לא אמרו אלא דשמוה בי תרי
notes.he: כלו' הא דאמרן פחות מכדי אונאה חוזר פי' חוזר ההדיוט להקדש אונאתו מיהו חילול הוי וקשה דמשמע פרק הנחנקין (סנהדרין דף פח.) גבי זקן ממרא דאפי' צנורא של הקדש צריך עשרה בני אדם לפדותו ומוקי התם דפליגי זקן ממרא וסנהדרין בפלוגתא דרבי אליעזר ורבנן בהקדשן וקאמר התם דלא מחייב אא"כ פליג זקן ממרא אסנהדרין בדבר שיש בו חיוב חטאת ומפרש לה התם כשנפדה ההקדש בג' לר"א אינו פדוי והוה הקדש ואי קידש בו האשה אח"כ אינה מקודשת ולרבנן הוי פדוי ויצא לחולין ואם קידש בו האשה מקודשת אלמא דשלשה ועשרה למר כדאית ליה ולמר כדאית ליה מעכבין והכא משמע דהוי מחולל בתרי ועוד שמואל היכי קאמר דמחולל על שוה פרוטה וצריך לומר דהכא מיירי בבעל הבית הפודה הקדש שלו וכי האי גוונא אמר שמואל דמחולל על פחות משוויו אבל גזבר המוכר הקדש צריך שלשה או עשרה למר כדאית ליה ולמר כדאית ליה:
notes.en: In brief: “They said only where two assessed it” refers to what was said, that even less than the measure of exploitation is returned: the layman returns the shortfall to the Temple, yet the desacralization stands. The difficulty: the chapter HaNeḥnakin (Sanhedrin 88a), on the rebellious elder, implies that even a drainpipe of consecrated property requires ten people to redeem it. It establishes there that the elder and the Sanhedrin disagree as in the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis about the assessment of consecrated property, since the elder is liable only for a matter that carries liability for a sin offering: if the property was redeemed by three, according to Rabbi Eliezer it is not redeemed and remains consecrated, so that if one afterward betrothed a woman with it she is not betrothed, while according to the Rabbis it is redeemed and goes out to non-sacred status, and she is betrothed. Evidently three, or ten, each according to his view, are indispensable, yet here it implies that it is desacralized by two. Further, how could Shmuel say it is desacralized on a peruta’s worth? One must say that here it speaks of an owner redeeming his own consecrated property, and in such a case Shmuel said it is desacralized for less than its value; but a treasurer selling consecrated property requires three or ten, each according to his view. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: דצריך לעשות לו דמים כדי שלא יתאנה הקדש אלא שלא נישום הקדש בשלשה כשאמר זו מחולל על זו אבל נשום בשלשה אינו חוזר ואין צריך לעשות לו דמים שוב:
notes.en: They taught only: that he must conduct an appraisal, so that the consecrated property should not be wronged, only where the consecrated property was not assessed by three when he said “This is desacralized onto this”; but if it was assessed by three, it is not reversed, and he need not conduct an appraisal again.

messages.text: Is that so? But didn’t Rav Safra say:
messages.quote: even if afterward one hundred people came … one need not return the disparity

messages.text: Where did one say the ruling that one hundred witnesses are like two witnesses, and two witnesses are like one hundred witnesses? That principle applies specifically to the matter of testimony. But with regard to the matter of assessments, we follow the majority of opinions.

notes.dh: והאמר רב ספרא היכא אמר מאה עדים כתרין
notes.he: כלומר [אם] (אין) מכחישין מאה עדים שני עדים חשובין הללו שנים כאותן מאה שאין מאמינין לאלו יותר מאלו הואיל [ואין] מזימין אותן:
notes.en: But didn’t Rav Safra say: Where does one say that a hundred witnesses are like two? That is, [if] a hundred witnesses contradict two witnesses, these two are considered like those hundred, for we do not believe these more than those, since they do not render them conspiring witnesses.

notes.dh: אבל לענין אומדנא אזלינן בתר רוב דעות
notes.he: אע"ג דנשום בשלשה לכתחלה:
notes.en: But with regard to assessment we follow the majority of opinions: even though it was assessed by three at first.

messages.text: If so, in Ulla’s case, one should follow the assessment of the one hundred and pay the disparity to the Temple treasury.

And furthermore, even in a case where three people initially assessed the value of the consecrated property, and afterward three other people assessed the consecrated property at a higher value, don’t we follow the latter assessment? Isn’t there is a principle that the Temple treasury of consecrated property always has the advantage?

notes.he: כלומר אפי' לא אתו אלא תלתא ואכחישו לתלתא קמאי יד ההקדש על העליונה ובתר בתראי אזלינן:
notes.en: And even three and three: [Rashi’s text reads “And even,” where ours reads “And furthermore.”] That is, even if only three came and contradicted the first three, the hand of the consecrated property is uppermost and we follow the latter ones.

notes.dh: ותו אפילו לא הויא אלא תלתא ותלתא
notes.he: ותלתא בתראי מטפן בשומא מי לא אזלינן בתר בתרא אלא עולא דאמר אבל נישום בשלשה אינו חוזר סבר לה כר' יוחנן כו':
notes.en: And furthermore, even if there were only three and three, and the latter three add to the assessment, don’t we follow the latter? Rather, Ulla, who said that if it was assessed by three it is not reversed, holds in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan, etc.

messages.text: Ulla holds that the halakha that the owner is required to conduct an appraisal, to ascertain the relative value of the two animals and to pay the difference to the Temple treasury, applies by rabbinic law, not by Torah law, and the Sages were lenient with regard to all rabbinic laws. Therefore, even if one hundred people assessed the value of the consecrated property at a higher value than the earlier assessment, one is not required to pay the disparity in value to the Temple treasury.

notes.he: לא אמרן דצריך לעשות לו דמים שוב אלא דשמוי לכתחלה בתרי אבל דשמוי בתלתא אע"ג דאתאן בי מאה ומטפו [לא הדרי ולא אמרי'] (לאהדר אמר) דהני תלת לא ליהוי עדיף שומייהו מדתרי (אלא אי) [ואי] אתו אחריני ומטפו ליהדר קמ"ל דלא הדר כיון דשמוי בתלת (הני והאמר רב ספרא אפילו למ"ד כו'):
notes.en: Another version: We said that he must conduct an appraisal again only where it was assessed at first by two; but where it was assessed by three, even if a hundred come and add, it is not reversed. And one should not say that the assessment of these three should be no better than that of two, so that if others come and add it should be reversed; it teaches us that it is not reversed, since it was assessed by three. [The printed text adds a garbled phrase: “But didn’t Rav Safra say: even according to the one who says, etc.”]

messages.text: Mishna
If one said: This non-sacred animal is hereby in place of a burnt offering, or: It is in place of a sin offering, he has said nothing, as he did not say that it was in place of a specific offering.

notes.he: הרי זו תחת חטאת או תחת עולה ואין לו לא חטאת ולא עולה עדיין לא אמר כלום:
notes.en: This is hereby in place of a sin offering, or in place of a burnt offering, and he has neither a sin offering nor a burnt offering: he has still said nothing.

messages.text: If he said: It is in place of this sin offering, or: It is in place of this burnt offering, or if he said: It is in place of a sin offering that I have in the house, or: It is in place of a burnt offering that I have in the house, and he had that offering in his house, his statement stands, i.e., is effective.

notes.he: שהיתה חטאת עומדת לפניו:
notes.en: Mishna. This one in place of this sin offering: that the sin offering was standing before him.

notes.he: [ואם אמר] תחת חטאת או תחת חטאת שיש לו בביתו דבריו קיימין:
notes.en: [And if he said]: in place of a sin offering, or in place of a sin offering that he has in his house, his statement stands.

messages.text: If he said with regard to a non-kosher animal and with regard to a blemished animal: These animals are hereby designated as a burnt offering, he has said nothing.
If he said: These animals are hereby designated for a burnt offering, the animals should be sold, and he brings a burnt offering purchased with the money received from their sale.

notes.he: משמע לדמי עולה דאי אינהו גופייהו הוא בעי לאקרובי הוה אמר הרי אלו עולה:
notes.en: These are hereby for a burnt offering: [this] implies for the value of a burnt offering, for if he had wanted to sacrifice them themselves, he would have said: These are hereby a burnt offering.

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, as, if it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, didn’t Rabbi Meir say: A person does not utter a statement for naught. In other words, if one issues a statement that cannot be fulfilled as stated, it is interpreted in a manner that renders it relevant. Consequently, when he said: This non-sacred animal is in place of a burnt offering, he must have been referring to a burnt offering that he had in his house.
messages.quote: This non-sacred animal is hereby in place of a burnt offering … he has said nothing

notes.he: דקתני תחת חטאת תחת עולה לא אמר כלום דלא כר"מ דאמר נותן דמיו כמה שהוא ראוי לימכר בשוק שאדם יודע שאין ערך לפחות מבן חדש וגמר ואמר לשם דמים:
notes.en: Gemara. The mishna: which teaches “in place of a sin offering, in place of a burnt offering, he has said nothing,” is not in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who says [of one who pledged the valuation of an infant less than a month old] that he gives its value, as much as it is fit to be sold for in the market; for a person knows that there is no valuation for one less than a month old, and he resolved and spoke for the sake of [its] value.

notes.he: פירוש דקתני תחת חטאת תחת עולה לא אמר כלום וכיון דאמר רבי מאיר אין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה הכי נמי הכא דעתיה אחטאת שיש לו בבית או אעולה שיש לו בבית הוציא דבריו ועוד יש מפרשים דקאי אהא דקתני אם אמר על בהמה טמאה ועל בעלת מום הרי אלו עולה לא אמר כלום והיינו דלא כרבי מאיר דכיון דאין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה דעתיה לומר הרי לעולה וגמר ואמר לשם דמים:
notes.en: The mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Meir: that is, [the clause] that teaches “in place of a sin offering, in place of a burnt offering, he has said nothing”; for since Rabbi Meir says that a person does not utter his words for naught, so too here his intention was for the sin offering that he has at home or the burnt offering that he has at home. And some also explain that it refers to what it teaches: if he said about a non-kosher animal and about a blemished animal “These are hereby a burnt offering,” he has said nothing. This is not in accordance with Rabbi Meir, for since a person does not utter his words for naught, his intention was to say “for a burnt offering,” and he resolved and spoke for the sake of [its] value.

notes.dh: דאי ר"מ האמר אין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה
notes.he: וגמר ואמר לשום דמיו הכא נמי סבירא ליה דתימכר:
notes.en: For if [it were] Rabbi Meir, didn’t he say: A person does not utter his words for naught, and he resolved and spoke for the sake of its value? Here too he would hold that it is sold.

messages.text: The reason that these animals are sold is that they are non-kosher and blemished animals, which are not fit to be sacrificed, and therefore they do not require the development of a blemish for them to be sold. But in the case of one who separates a female animal for a guilt offering or for a burnt offering, which may be brought only from males, since a female animal is fit to be sacrificed as a different type of offering, the animal does require the development of a blemish for it to be sold.
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches: If he said with regard to a non-kosher animal and with regard to a blemished animal: These animals are hereby designated for a burnt offering, the animals should be sold, and he brings a burnt offering purchased with the money received from their sale.
messages.quote: These animals are hereby designated for a burnt offering, the animals should be sold

notes.he: לא בעיין לרעות דהא מסאבי וקיימי:
notes.en: They do not require a blemish: they do not require grazing, for they are already standing disqualified.

notes.dh: הא מפריש נקבה כו' בעיא מומא
notes.he: הואיל וחזיא להקרבת שלמים:
notes.en: But one who separates a female, etc., requires a blemish: since it is fit to be sacrificed as a peace offering.

notes.dh: טעמא דאמר על בהמה טמאה דעל בעלת מום
notes.he: ימכרו לאלתר בלא דעתיה משום דהא מסאבי וקיימי אבל מפריש נקבה לאשם בעיא מומא קודם שתמכר:
notes.en: The reason is that he said it about a non-kosher animal and about a blemished animal: they are sold at once [the text adds the unclear words “without his intent”], because they are already standing disqualified; but one who separates a female for a guilt offering requires a blemish before it is sold.

notes.he: ל"א אבל אמר על נקבה הרי זו לעולה קדשה קדושת הגוף לעולה ותמכר ועושה תמורה מגו דחזיא לגופיה לשלמים:
notes.en: Another version: But if he said about a female “This is hereby for a burnt offering,” it is consecrated with inherent sanctity as a burnt offering, and it is sold, and it renders a substitute, since its body is fit [to be sacrificed] as a peace offering.

messages.text: Consequently: The mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, as we learned in a mishna (19b) that
messages.quote: one who separates a female animal for a guilt offering or for a burnt offering … does require the development of a blemish

notes.he: דאמר בפ' אלו קדשים (לעיל תמורה דף יט:) המפריש נקבה לאשם תמכר שלא במום. לישנא אחרינא קדש גופא דבעיא לרעות דלא כר"ש דאמר בפ' אלו קדשים אף לעולתו אינו עושה תמורה אלמא לא קדיש לגופיה:
notes.en: Not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon: who says in the chapter Elu Kodashim (above, Temurah 19b): One who separates a female for a guilt offering, it is sold without a blemish. Another version: [the mishna implies that a female designated for a burnt offering] is itself sacred, so that it requires grazing; [this is] not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who says in the chapter Elu Kodashim: even for his burnt offering it does not render a substitute, which shows that it itself does not become sacred.

messages.text: In the case of one who designates a female animal for a guilt offering, since a female is unfit to be sacrificed as that offering, its halakhic status is like that of a blemished animal in the sense that it does not become inherently sacred; rather, only its value is sacred. Therefore, it may be sold without it having developed a blemish, and a guilt offering is purchased with the money received from its sale.

notes.he: דאמר לעיל בפרק אלו קדשים אף לעולה אין עושין תמורה דלית ליה מגו ולית ליה שם עולה על אמו:
notes.en: And not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda, where ours reads Rabbi Shimon], who said above in the chapter Elu Kodashim: even for a burnt offering they do not render a substitute, for he does not accept the reasoning of “since,” and does not hold that the name “burnt offering” [applies] to its mother.

notes.he: הדרן עלך כיצד מערימין
notes.en: Hadran alakh Keitzad Ma’arimin: we will return to you, “How One Employs Artifice.”

Chapter 6 · כל האסורין · Kol HaAsurin: animals whose sacrifice upon the altar is prohibited, and how they render a mixture of animals prohibited.

Continues on 28a with the chapter’s opening mishna: all animals whose sacrifice on the altar is prohibited render a mixture prohibited in any amount: an animal that copulated with a person or was the object of bestiality, one set aside for or worshipped as an idol, the payment to a prostitute or the price of a dog, an animal of diverse kinds, a tereifa, and one born by caesarean section.
